method: One conversion for every country, the one behind the Western Europe and Buenos Aires presets. Take unplanned SAIFI (interruptions per customer a year) and CAIDI (SAIDI / SAIFI) without major or exceptional events, for urban customers where a source gives them. Assume interruption lengths are log-normal with sigma 1.2 and mean equal to CAIDI, so the share lasting 4 hours or more is S4 = 1 - Phi((ln 4 - ln CAIDI + 0.72) / 1.2). Rate of long local outages = SAIFI x S4, times 0.9 where the figure is national (the AHS 2023 urban/all ratio for the United States); add a rate for same-day system-wide blackouts that the indices exclude (1.15% a year in Europe as in the preset, 0.3-1% elsewhere in the rich world, 0.5-5% in middle-income countries from each grid's record); probability = 1 - exp(-rate). The 4-hour threshold is what the Western Europe and Buenos Aires anchors used; applied to EIA's United States indices it also reproduces the AHS-based 0.11, so it is the conversion that puts all three anchors on one scale (at 6 hours the same indices give about half). Inputs: CEER Benchmarking Report 6.1 (2014-16 means, the Western Europe anchor's source) for 22 European countries; EIA for the United States; national regulators or utilities for Canada, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, China, Indonesia and the Philippines; the World Bank Doing Business 2020 SAIDI and SAIFI (largest business city, 2018-19) for the rest and as a cross-check everywhere; Enterprise Surveys (share of firms with outages 2023-25, outages a month in older rounds) as a further check. Ranges divide and multiply the rate by 2 (good data), 2.5 or 3 (poor data). durationFactor is the mean length of a 4-hour-plus outage under the same log-normal at the country's CAIDI divided by the same at the preset's reference CAIDI (United States 2.0 h, Western Europe 0.83 h, Buenos Aires 1.9 h); it moves much less than CAIDI itself because every counted outage is already at least 4 hours long. Where the source covers only the largest city or old years, the range is wider.

reproduced.basis: EIA 2021-25 without major event days: SAIFI 1.02-1.09 (mean 1.06), CAIDI 116-124 min (2.0 h) (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/annual/html/epa_11_01.html). S4 = 12.0%, rate 0.127, plus 0.008 for system-wide blackouts (2003 Northeast), times 0.9 urban = 0.113.

anchors.comment: Preset 0.11 (0.06-0.16) came from the AHS 2023 household survey (17.7% with a 6 h+ outage less 6.9% regional events). The SAIDI/SAIFI route gives 0.113, within 3%. At a 6-hour threshold the same indices would give 0.066: the survey shows far more long outages than a log-normal fitted to non-major-event indices implies, and the 4-hour threshold happens to absorb that gap.

localOutage.probability.basis: Enterprise Surveys: 32.8 outages a month for firms in 2014 (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/power-outages-in-firms-per-month) and 82% of firms with an outage in 2025 (https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/NGA/indicator/IC.ELC.OUTG.ZS); the grid collapsed almost monthly in 2024 and again in December 2025 and January 2026 (https://allafrica.com/stories/202602020399.html). A 4 h+ cut in a year is close to certain; Band A customers are the exception.

localOutage.durationFactor.basis: Most urban customers get well under 20 h of supply a day and failed transformers wait weeks; no CAIDI found.

countries.notes: Doing Business reported no SAIDI or SAIFI. The rate is dozens of long outages a year; a probability capped at 1 cannot carry it.

countries.name: Philippines

localOutage.probability.basis: Meralco 2024: SAIFI 1.041, SAIDI 108.2 min, CAIDI 1.73 h (https://philstar.com/headlines/2025/03/20/2429561/through-innovative-and-cutting-edge-initiatives-meralco-drives-transformative-energy-future). Other cities worse: urban SAIFI 1.6, CAIDI 1.8 h, S4 10.3% = 0.165, + 0.03 for island-grid blackouts (Panay, January 2024) = 0.18.

countries.notes: Typhoon outages belong to hurricane. Doing Business 2020 Manila: SAIDI 3.57 h, SAIFI 2.23.

countries.name: South Africa

localOutage.probability.basis: No load shedding since 16 May 2025 (504 days on 4 October 2026; load reduction 2.8% of Eskom customers, https://www.sanews.gov.za/node/84735). Doing Business 2020 Johannesburg: SAIDI 30.5 h, SAIFI 5.98 (CAIDI 5.1 h) gives 0.87, but that year had load shedding. Municipal network failures in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni remain frequent; Cape Town is reliable.

localOutage.durationFactor.basis: CAIDI 5.1 h gives 1.39 by the formula; raised for slow municipal repairs (cable theft, substation failures lasting days).

countries.notes: If load shedding returns, the probability goes toward 1. Enterprise Surveys 2020: 7.7 firm outages a month, 92% of firms.

openQuestions: Threshold: BRIEF-COUNTRIES defines localOutage at 6 hours, but the Western Europe and Buenos Aires anchors were built at 4 hours and the US anchor from a 6-hour survey. I used 4 hours on non-major-event indices because it reproduces all three anchors; at 6 hours the same indices give about half. The definition text should say which scale the presets are on.

Saturation: localOutage is one event a year at most. For Nigeria (dozens of long cuts a year), India outside the metros, South Africa, Turkey, Colombia and Brazil the rate of 4 h+ cuts approaches or exceeds one a year, so the model understates their harm. A rate field (expected events a year) would fix this; the rates are in the notes or recoverable as -ln(1 - p).

Heat-wave overlap: the Buenos Aires anchor subtracted heat-wave cuts (7.5%) because the preset's heatWave carries its own power window. For the other middle-income countries I subtracted nothing; where their indices include heat-driven cuts (India, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey) a household with hot summers ticked double-counts some outages.

The 0.9 urban factor is the US survey ratio for any outage; for countries whose national indices are dominated by rural overhead lines (Poland, the Baltics, the Nordic countries, Canada) a city flat's risk is probably lower still. Doing Business largest-city figures, given in the notes, suggest by how much.

Sabotage and war damage (Berlin arson 2025-26, strikes on Israeli infrastructure) were treated as local outages with small allowances; the AI researchers' cyberOutage or the war hazards may already cover part of them.

Checker: India's 0.55 rests on snippets (an online household poll and CSRD hours of supply). Enterprise Surveys, which the method uses as a cross-check, show 19.9% (2022) and 15.4% (2025) of Indian firms with any outage in the year (https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/IND/indicator/IC.ELC.OUTG.ZS), against 22.6% in the United States and 56.6% in Australia. That series ranks countries erratically, so it does not settle the figure, but it points below 0.55 rather than above.
